questions.question: Describe how concrete and plaster of Paris are made, and give one use of each.
questions.expected_answer: Both are mixed with water and then set hard. Concrete is made by mixing cement, sand, stone and water; it sets in hours and gets stronger for weeks. It is used for floors, foundations, bridges and dams. Plaster of Paris is a white powder mixed with water that sets in minutes; it is used for casts on broken bones, moulds and ornaments.

questions.question: Name the method used to make each of these: glue paste, bread and jelly.
questions.expected_answer: Glue paste is made by mixing flour and water. Bread is made by mixing and cooking: the dough is mixed and baked. Jelly is made by mixing and cooling: the powder is mixed with hot water and cooled until it sets.

questions.question: Explain the steps in making a fired clay brick, and why firing is important.
questions.expected_answer: Clay is mixed with water, pressed into moulds, then dried in the sun or sheds, and finally fired in a kiln at a very high temperature. Firing makes the brick very hard and strong, and stops it from going soft again when it gets wet.
